correctness.rationale: For one mode, the exchangeability constraints reduce exactly to two scalar sector parameters \(u,v\in[-1,1]\). A parity-preserving Gaussian copy rotation diagonalizes the retained two-copy covariance while leaving the product marginal invariant. The resulting commuting two-mode states reduce to two Bernoulli products, whose four probability differences give the exact trace norm \(2|h|+2h^2\) with \(h=(u-v)/(2n)\). Maximization over \(|u-v|\le2\) is exact and the anchor paper supplies a feasible extremal extension. The finite verifier only corroborates the algebra.

value.rationale: This is the exact finite-n constant for the first nontrivial retained marginal in the minimal local fermionic Gaussian system. It quantifies precisely how much slack is introduced when the anchor theorem converts its sharp covariance suppression through a general perturbation inequality, showing an asymptotic factor-of-two gap and classifying all extremizers. The object and invariant are canonical within the new de Finetti theorem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
